messages.subject: R to/java - passing data.frames back and forth
messages.subject_clean: R to/java - passing data.frames back and forth
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I want to pass data.frames from R to java.
Is there is a standard way to do this, when the colums contain 
basis types like integer, logical, character and double?

I didn't find any examples in the rJava docs or via google.
Did I miss something?
Is there is a package which contains relevant code that I could emulate?

For example, a data.frame with columns containing 
integers and doubles can be passed to java and recalled to R.

# construct a data.frame
df <- expand.grid(a = 2:3, b = letters[2:3], cc = c(T,F), d = 1:2 + 0.0)
df$b <- as.character(df$b)
str(df)
head(df)
# generate the java object that corresponds to a data.frame(?)
(lst <- .jarray(lapply(df, .jarray)))
# look up the data.frame inside java
lstRefs <- lapply(.jevalArray(lst), .jcastToArray)
# get the column of integers and doubles.
.jevalArray(lstRefs[[1]])
.jevalArray(lstRefs[[4]])

# strings work but return a list so additional functionality seems
essential
unlist(lapply(.jevalArray(lstRefs[[2]]), .jsimplify))
# Logicals do not work as I expected.
.jevalArray(lstRefs[[4]])
# -- don't know how to evaluate an array with signature [Z .

Because of the different treatment for strings and logicals, 
I get the impression that my approach is not very robust. 
Is there something obvious that I am missing?

Regards,

John.

messages.subject_clean: JGR linux installation problem - no java.h
messages.body_plain:
Craig, thanks for your help on this.  Actually it was javah that was
missing, not java.h.  Also it was complaining about jni.h.  I installed
JDK as you suggested (btw your link was to JRE, not JDK).  I'm sure
NetBeans had already put it somewhere but never mind.  After a bit of
searching and fiddling I worked out that I had to point JAVA_HOME to
/usr/java/default, after which the installation could find the files and
ran through nicely.

Thanks
Richard

messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon,

Thanks for that information.
I have recompiled 0.4-14 (as it hasn't appeared on CRAN yet
http://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/checkSummary.html).

The code now works as expected, thanks.

Regards,

John.

-----Original Message-----
From: Simon Urbanek [mailto:urbanek at research.att.com] 
Sent: 21 February 2007 22:57
To: Gavin, John
Cc: stats-rosuda-devel at listserv.uni-augsburg.de
Subject: Re: [stats-rosuda-devel] R to/java - passing data.frames back
and forth

John,

your approach is correct - you have just uncovered a bug and a  
missing feature ;). Thanks for reporting this.

I have fixed it in 0.4-14 now (now obtainable from
http://www.rforge.net/rJava/files/
later on CRAN) and in the current development version of rJava (0.5).  
As the name implies the latter  is still experimental, so you may  
want to try 0.4-14 first.

Cheers,
Simon


On Feb 14, 2007, at 8:31 AM, <john.gavin at ubs.com>  
<john.gavin at ubs.com> wrote:

> Hi,
>
> I want to pass data.frames from R to java.
> Is there is a standard way to do this, when the colums contain
> basis types like integer, logical, character and double?
>
> I didn't find any examples in the rJava docs or via google.
> Did I miss something?
> Is there is a package which contains relevant code that I could  
> emulate?
>
> For example, a data.frame with columns containing
> integers and doubles can be passed to java and recalled to R.
>
> # construct a data.frame
> df <- expand.grid(a = 2:3, b = letters[2:3], cc = c(T,F), d = 1:2 +  
> 0.0)
> df$b <- as.character(df$b)
> str(df)
> head(df)
> # generate the java object that corresponds to a data.frame(?)
> (lst <- .jarray(lapply(df, .jarray)))
> # look up the data.frame inside java
> lstRefs <- lapply(.jevalArray(lst), .jcastToArray)
> # get the column of integers and doubles.
> .jevalArray(lstRefs[[1]])
> .jevalArray(lstRefs[[4]])
>
> # strings work but return a list so additional functionality seems
> essential
> unlist(lapply(.jevalArray(lstRefs[[2]]), .jsimplify))
> # Logicals do not work as I expected.
> .jevalArray(lstRefs[[4]])
> # -- don't know how to evaluate an array with signature [Z .
>
> Because of the different treatment for strings and logicals,
> I get the impression that my approach is not very robust.
> Is there something obvious that I am missing?
>
> Regards,
>
> John.

messages.subject: Re: JGR: Problems with decimal numers
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I've got an update to the problem described in the last mail.

First, it is limited to java6, after switching back to java5, the
problem is gone (but I'm missing the nice look of JGR running with
java6 ;-) ).

And then it seems to be a general problem with the decimal point. JGR
seems to use the comma as the decimal point, what could be due to the
locale setting of the OS (just a guess). But this causes various
problems as described.

When I wrote an PDF file (with the pdf()-device, not saving from
JavaGD), the Adobe Reader told me:

        An unrecognized token '0,302' was found.

and the file was empty. So it seems that the comma is even used inside
the pdf where it must not occur.

Maybe this could help you finding out what goes wrong here.

Regards,
Frederik
